answer: At activation the registry gives each identity one unique erasure-coded shard, keyed by hash(pubkey||epoch seed), kept in a haven: an endpoint that must answer random reads inside a deadline too short to re-fetch. One challenge thread per identity lets offsets wander over the whole shard; each reply is checked against the shard's Merkle root. Shards differ per key, so puppets cannot share bytes: 1,000 puppets store 1,000 shards and serve 1,000 threads, no bulk discount, while an honest agent stores one shard once. A missed read burns the accrued credit.
